source: Wasserportal Berlin (daily mean water temperature, Land Berlin) and Geoportal Berlin (district and water outlines, dl-de/zero-2-0)
unit: decametres from 368000 E / 5798000 N, ETRS89 UTM 33N

lakes.name: Orankesee
lakes.note: Swimming is legal only inside the Strandbad, which is shut for the season. The Berliner Seehunde club swims there on Sunday mornings; its trial-swim list is closed at the moment.

lakes.name: Plötzensee
lakes.note: Legal only inside the Strandbad area, which stays closed until May. Read this gauge as the small, sheltered city lake it is.

lakes.name: Halensee
lakes.note: Legal only from the Strandbad, inside the buoyed strip on the east shore. Out of season this is a reading, not an invitation.

lakes.name: Flughafensee
lakes.note: Legal only in the parts marked with buoys and signs. The gauge sat at freezing point for more than a week in February 2026.

lakes.name: Groß Glienicker See
lakes.note: The whole lake is listed bathing water, with a north and a south spot. This gauge never dropped under 4 °C in either winter.

lakes.name: Havel at Tegelort
lakes.note: The Havel around Tegeler See and Heiligensee is open to swimmers, but never in the shipping channel or within 100 m of a bridge.

lakes.name: Havel near Wannsee
lakes.note: Gauge at Pfaueninsel, the closest one to the Unterhavel beaches such as Kleine Badewiese and Große Steinlanke. Keep well clear of the shipping channel.

lakes.name: Müggelsee outflow
lakes.note: The gauge sits at the Rahnsdorf ferry, where the lake drains into the Müggelspree. Swim from the Müggelsee shore, never within 50 m of a ferry or landing.

lakes.name: Zeuthener See
lakes.note: The Dahme lakes are listed bathing water and Schmöckwitz has its own bathing spot. Stay out of the boat lanes.
